citations.label: OpenAI, Advancing coding in low-resource programming languages (scope)
citations.excerpt: Our latest model advances bring stronger capabilities for building and migrating software in low-resource programming languages such as COBOL, Fortran, and Visual Basic.

citations.label: OpenAI, Advancing coding in low-resource programming languages (data scarcity)
citations.excerpt: These languages have less code and documentation available for models to learn from than languages like Python and JavaScript, yet support critical infrastructure and essential services around the world.

citations.label: OpenAI, Advancing coding in low-resource programming languages (customer reports)
citations.excerpt: This work is guided by feedback from developers and enterprise customers who have told us that coding models often struggle with these languages.

citations.label: OpenAI, Advancing coding in low-resource programming languages (MultiLangBench task)
citations.excerpt: MultiLangBench tests whether a model can build a SQLite-compatible database engine from scratch across 20 different programming languages.

citations.label: OpenAI, Advancing coding in low-resource programming languages (reference oracle)
citations.excerpt: We use the reference SQLite implementation to check whether the resulting database has the expected contents.

citations.label: OpenAI, Advancing coding in low-resource programming languages (per-language results)
citations.excerpt: Improvements extend to every language tested, including COBOL (10.9% to 72.1%), OCaml (25.6% to 85.8%), Fortran (21.4% to 83.5%), and Visual Basic (27.5% to 89.4%).

citations.label: OpenAI, Advancing coding in low-resource programming languages (hardest language)
citations.excerpt: Astra scores above 83% in 19 of the 20 languages, with COBOL remaining the hardest at 72%.

citations.label: OpenAI, Advancing coding in low-resource programming languages (migration oracle)
citations.excerpt: To test whether these behaviors are preserved, we evaluate our models on hidden tests that require byte-for-byte parity on observable outputs.
